title: Exact free extension from a semisimplicial component
statement:
Let $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$, the small ringed sites $(\mathcal C_n,\mathcal O_n)$, the total module category $\mathscr M$, and the evaluations $e_n$ be as in [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category], with all its size and coherence hypotheses. Assume every transition module pullback $f_\alpha^*$ is exact. For an object $E$ of $\mathscr M$ write $\theta^E_\alpha:f_\alpha^*E_m\to E_n$ for its transition along $\alpha:[m]\hookrightarrow[n]$, and for $E\in D(\mathscr M)$ write $\theta^E_\alpha:Lf_\alpha^*e_mE\to e_nE$ for the derived transition of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. For $p\ge0$ and an $\mathcal O_p$-module sheaf $G$, define a system $\ell_pG$ by
$$(\ell_pG)_m=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[p]\hookrightarrow[m]}f_\alpha^*G.$$
The empty sum is zero. The transition for $\beta:[m]\hookrightarrow[k]$ carries the $\alpha$ summand to the $\beta\alpha$ summand through the specified pullback composition isomorphism. These formulas define an exact additive functor $\ell_p:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_p)\to\mathscr M$ left adjoint to $e_p$. Restriction to the identity-labelled summand in component $p$ gives its adjunction bijection; the inverse of $u:G\to E_p$ sends the $\alpha$ summand to $\theta^E_\alpha f_\alpha^*u$.
The termwise functors on unbounded cochain complexes induce an adjunction on the unbounded derived categories, with natural bijections, for $G\in D(\mathcal O_p)$ and $E\in D(\mathscr M)$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathscr M)}(\ell_pG,E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_p)}(G,e_pE).$$
The component formula and the inverse-adjunct formula above hold in these derived categories with $f_\alpha^*=Lf_\alpha^*$, and $e_p\ell_p\cong\mathrm{id}$ is the identity-summand identification. For $E\in D(\mathscr M)$, the counit $\ell_pe_pE\to E$ has components the derived transition maps on the labelled summands.

proof.text: Put $I_{p,m}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}}([p],[m])$; this set is finite, and empty for $m<p$. The module categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so the finite sums in the statement exist. Denote the summand inclusions by $i_\alpha$ and the coherent composition comparison by $c_{\beta,\alpha}:f_\beta^*f_\alpha^*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{\beta\alpha}^*$. Pullback is additive by the exactness assumption; it preserves finite biproducts, since it preserves their inclusion/projection identities. Define $t_\beta$ by $t_\beta f_\beta^*(i_\alpha)=i_{\beta\alpha}c_{\beta,\alpha}$. On the $\alpha$ summand the two composites for $\beta$ followed by $\gamma$ agree by the associativity coherence equation for $c$; identity coherence gives the identity transition. The systems description in [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] therefore makes this an object of $\mathscr M$. For $v:G\to H$ define $(\ell_pv)_m$ on the $\alpha$ summand by $i_\alpha f_\alpha^*v$. Naturality of $c$ gives compatibility with $t_\beta$. Identities, composition and addition hold on each summand, proving additive functoriality.

Write $\Phi(h)=h_p i_{\mathrm{id}}:G\to E_p$, using $f_{\mathrm{id}}^*G\cong G$. Given $u:G\to E_p$, define $\Psi(u)_m i_\alpha=\theta^E_\alpha f_\alpha^*u$. For $\beta:[m]\hookrightarrow[k]$, compatibility of the transitions of $E$ says $\theta^E_\beta f_\beta^*(\theta^E_\alpha)=\theta^E_{\beta\alpha}c_{\beta,\alpha}$. Naturality of $c$ then proves the required morphism-of-systems equation for $\Psi(u)$ on every summand. Identity compatibility gives $\Phi\Psi(u)=u$. Conversely, compatibility of any $h:\ell_pG\to E$ along $\alpha:[p]\hookrightarrow[m]$, applied to the identity summand, gives $h_mi_\alpha=\theta^E_\alpha f_\alpha^*(h_pi_{\mathrm{id}})$, hence $\Psi\Phi(h)=h$. These formulas commute with precomposition in $G$ and postcomposition in $E$, giving the asserted natural adjunction.

source.place: Tag 0D72, lemma-restriction-module-to-components-site, direct adjunction verification; agent adaptation

proof.text: An injective order-preserving self-map of the finite ordinal $[p]$ is bijective and must send its successive elements to themselves. Thus $I_{p,p}=\{\mathrm{id}\}$ and $e_p\ell_pG\cong f_{\mathrm{id}}^*G\cong G$. In the bijection just constructed the unit is the inverse of this identification. Taking $u=\mathrm{id}_{E_p}$ shows that the counit has restriction $\theta^E_\alpha$ to the $\alpha$ summand. This also specifies the unit and counit, rather than merely choosing an abstract adjunction with the same functors.

source.place: Tag 0D72, lemma-restriction-module-to-components-site; identity-only summand is special to injective order maps

proof.text: For a short exact sequence of modules on $\mathcal C_p$, applying $f_\alpha^*$ gives a short exact sequence for each $\alpha$, by hypothesis. Their finite sum is short exact: its kernel and cokernel are the sums of the respective kernels and cokernels, as follows by taking each projection and then assembling the factorizations with the inclusions. This includes the empty sum, the zero sequence. Hence each $e_m\ell_p$ is exact. To detect exactness in $\mathscr M$, take the three-term complex associated to the image sequence. Its cohomology evaluates to zero in every component, because the evaluations in [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] are exact. Joint conservativity applied to each map $0\to H^q$ makes every such cohomology object zero. Thus $\ell_p$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 0D74, lemma-exactness-g-shriek-modules; finite-biproduct argument for the injective-order-map adaptation

proof.text: Apply part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to the additive adjunction $\ell_p\dashv e_p$. This gives the adjunction on all cochain complexes, with the termwise unit and counit from the preceding steps. Both functors are exact: $\ell_p$ by the previous step and $e_p$ by [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] supplies their functors on the unbounded derived categories and the natural comparison isomorphisms with termwise application. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] the two functors from complexes are localizations at quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to this adjunction on complexes and these comparison isomorphisms. It gives the derived adjunction, both triangle identities, and unit and counit induced from the original ones, hence the displayed natural Hom bijection. No boundedness or injective replacement is used.

source.place: Tag 0D9E, lemma-derived-cartesian-shriek, proof (2), first sentence; generic termwise/localization facts supplied by the cited nodes

proof.text: For a complex $K$ on $\mathcal C_p$, evaluation of the termwise extension is literally the complex $\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I_{p,m}} f_\alpha^*K$. Localize this equality using [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] for the exact pullbacks, evaluations and finite-sum functor. Finite biproducts pass to derived categories: their inclusions and projections satisfy $\pi_\alpha i_\delta=\delta_{\alpha\delta}$ and $\sum i_\alpha\pi_\alpha=1$, which still hold after the additive localization. These equations also show that an additive functor preserves the same biproduct. The resulting component formula is therefore $e_m\ell_pG\cong\bigoplus_\alpha Lf_\alpha^*G$, naturally in arbitrary derived $G$, with the transition comparisons obtained by localizing $c$. Exactness makes $Lf_\alpha^*$ the termwise pullback functor: by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] the localized termwise pullback is a left derived functor of $Q\circ C(f_\alpha^*)$, so it is $Lf_\alpha^*$ compatibly with the maps to $Q(f_\alpha^*K)$. So for $E$ represented by a complex $K$, the derived transition $\theta^E_\alpha$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] is the localized chain transition $f_\alpha^*K_m\to K_n$. The unit and counit formulas of [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] identify the localized unit with the identity-summand inclusion and the localized counit on the $\alpha$ summand with the derived transition $\theta^E_\alpha$ from [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category]. In particular the unit remains the inverse of $e_p\ell_p\cong\mathrm{id}$. Finally for an arbitrary derived morphism $u:G\to e_pE$, its inverse adjunct is $\varepsilon_E\circ\ell_pu$, whose $\alpha$ summand is $\theta^E_\alpha Lf_\alpha^*u$. This proves the claimed formulas for all derived morphisms, including those not represented by a map between the original complexes.
